Morphology General Habit Perennial herb to 2 m Vegetative Multiplication Corms Corm 5–6  c.2 cm, oblong Morphology Stem Stem scandent, 60–200 cm high, the basal 18 cm lacking leaf Morphology Leaves Leaves very numerous, set close together in whorls of 3–4, growing smaller and narrower towards stem apex, variable in width even on same plant, 10–17 0.5–3.5 cm, lanceolate or linear-lanceolate, tip drawn out into tendril c.2 cm long (included in leaf length) Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Flowers axillary, bright yellow or orange Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Pedicel Pedicel 2–5.5 cm, bent at apex so flowers are nodding Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Calyx Sepals and petals lanceolate, acute, united for 2–4 mm at base, 17–40 4–10 mm Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Androecium Stamens Filaments Filaments c.7 mm long; anther c.8 mm long Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Gynoecium Ovary Ovary 8–10 × 3 mm (possibly partly developed); style 4 mm long with 3 recurved branch 2–3 mm long. Distribution Zimbabwe, Mozambique. Also in South Africa and Swaziland. Ecology Woodland; 800–1500 m. Conservation Conservation notes Widespread and not threatened globally, but within the Flora area likely to be Vulnerable. NE Indigenous * * * * Overview * Gallery * Name * Classification * Literature * Records * Sequences * Uses Image Morphological description A scandent plant with a small tuber. Stems simple, glabrous. Leaves about 13 cm long, 0.8 to 1.2 cm. broad, lanceolate, long attenuated into a tendril, glabrous. Flowers solitary in the axils of the leaves. Pedicels up to 1 x 5 cm long, terete, glabrous. Perianth campanulate, 2-2 cm long, glabrous; tube very short; lobes lanceolate, acuminate, acute, with a prominent mid-rib. Stamens inserted at the base of the perianth-tube; filaments 3 mm long, flattened, linear; anthers 5 mm long, oblong. Ovary 6 mm long, ellipsoid, glabrous; style 3 mm long, terete; lobes 1-5 mm long, linear. From: Phillips, EP; Lansdell, KA. 1930. Littonia modesta Hook. Fl. Pl. South Africa 10: t.366 [CC BY] Climbing geophyte, 0.3-2.0 m high. Corms tunicated. Stems usually simple, scandent or erect. Leaves verticillate below, alternate above, linear to ovate, apex attenuated into a recurved tendril. Flowers cymose, on upper part of stem; pedicels long, arising beside a leaf or unattended; tepals equal, persistent, slightly saccate at base, yellow. Stamens short, filiform; anthers 2-thecous, erect, basifixed. Ovary ovoid, trigonous; ovules many. Flowering time Dec.-Feb. Fruit an ovoid capsule, 3-valved, loculicidal, leathery. Seed globose, fleshy, red, on long funicles. From: Bredenkamp, CL. 2019. Colchicaceae. In: CL Bredenkamp (ed.), A Flora of the Eastern Cape Province. Strelitzia 41(3): 1681-1687. South African National Biodiversity Institute, Pretoria. [CC BY] Climbing geophyte, up to 2 m high. Leaves cauline, verticillate below, alternate above; blade linear to ovate, ± 130 mm long, apex a recurved tendril or with an arista. Flowers: solitary; perianth with segments free, connate at base, apices pointed, recurved, golden-yellow; Nov.-Mar. From: Retief, E; Meyer, NL. 2017. Colchicaceae. In: E Retief & NL Meyer (eds), Plants of the Free State: Inventory and identification guide. Strelitzia 38: 868-872. South African National Biodiversity Institute, Pretoria.
